## Loupe & Lettres — créé avec l'aide de l'IA

### How it works
This manual workflow checks the totals of one invoice with integer arithmetic. Each line amount is rounded half-up to the cent; VAT is rounded by ONE rule you choose (vatRounding: per_group = once per VAT rate, the default, or per_line). It returns line amounts, VAT per rate, totals, a check against the total you stated (declaredTotal, optional), a suggested next number and a printable HTML page. The workflow adds no node that sends or stores data and needs no account, API, credential or AI model. Your n8n instance may keep the inputs and outputs in its execution history, depending on its configuration.

### Setup
Import this JSON into a fresh workflow and run it once with the synthetic invoice in “Example invoice”. Then replace invoiceNumber, issueDate (YYYY-MM-DD), currency (EUR, USD, GBP or CHF), lines (description, quantity up to 3 decimals, unitPrice up to 4 decimals, vatRate in percent) and optionally seller, buyer, declaredTotal and vatRounding. Quantities, prices and rates are plain non-negative decimals written as text, for example "19.99".

### Read this
The workflow stores no counter: suggestedNextNumber only increments the trailing digits of the number you give it. You must keep the real counter yourself and check that a number is unused. The HTML page is a layout, not a legal invoice validator: required mentions depend on your country and status. Not accounting or tax advice. To get a PDF, open the html field in a browser and print to PDF.
